page_metadata.title: A Physiologically Based Pharmacokinetic and Pharmacodynamic (PBPK/PD) Model of Dapagliflozin in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: The Effect of Dosing, Hepatorenal Impairment, and Food

model_classification.evidence_quote: Renal filtration and tubular glucose reabsorption were not modelled explicitly. Renal elimination of dapagliflozin (DAP) and its metabolite D3G was instead described using first-order processes, depending on kidney volume, renal function (glomerular filtration rate), and compound-specific excretion rate constants.

parameters.parameter_name: Scaling factor for renal function (f renal)

provenance.source_quote: Several key factors influencing pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic variability were implemented as scaling parameters. Renal impairment was modeled as a progressive decline in renal function using the factor f renal , which was applied to glomerular filtration rate (GFR) and renal clearance of dapagliflozin and D3G. Scaling values were mapped from KDIGO categories: normal (eGFR ≥ 90 mL/min, f renal = 1.00 ), mild (GFR 50–89 mL/min, f renal = 0.69 ), moderate (GFR 30–49 mL/min, f renal = 0.32 ), severe (GFR ≤30 mL/min, f renal = 0.19 ), derived from KDIGO guidelines and related modeling studies [ , ].

parameters.parameter_name: Reduction in absorption rate constant in fed state

provenance.source_quote: Food effects were incorporated by assuming a reduction in the absorption rate constant in the fed state. Specifically, the absorption rate was reduced by 70% relative to the fasted state (from 1.0 to 0.3).

parameters.parameter_name: Absorption rate constant in fed state

provenance.source_quote: Food effects were incorporated by assuming a reduction in the absorption rate constant in the fed state. Specifically, the absorption rate was reduced by 70% relative to the fasted state (from 1.0 to 0.3).

The pharmacokinetics (PK) of dapagliflozin are well characterized. It is rapidly absorbed, reaching peak plasma concentrations within 2 h, has a half-life of approximately 13 h, and an oral bioavailability of about 78%.
